clue.text: Plucky standby in the animal enclosure

parts.note: game, as in 'game for anything', means plucky or spirited
a reserve is a standby kept ready in case it is needed

explanation.surface: A brave substitute waits in the pen with the beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildlife park where wild animals are kept protected in a large fenced area is an enclosure for animals.

clue.text: Enliven morning service

parts.note: AM (ante meridiem) is the standard abbreviation for morning
use means service, as in 'of service' or 'of use'

explanation.surface: Something lively is wanted to brighten up a morning church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to cheer and enliven them.

clue.text: English clergyman building muscle

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar from England is working out at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' only links the wordplay to the definition, while hinting at muscle-building in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy names a muscle that raises a body part, such as a hair or the spine, by this term.

clue.text: Use ruse to get me up earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the turned-round me comes before the word for ruse
in a down clue, up means the word me is written bottom to top, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a ploy is a ruse or crafty move

explanation.surface: Someone is told to play a trick to get themselves out of bed sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage or make use of something is to put it to work.

clue.text: Discharge last of the task force

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word the

parts.note: a mission is a group of people sent abroad on a task, like a task force

explanation.surface: The final members of a military task force are sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests leaving the army, but it is the noun meaning something given off.
explanation.definitionFit: A release of gas, fluid or light is a discharge.

clue.text: Old and experienced doctor gets time and a quarter

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
an era is a period of time
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A doctor on overtime is paid time and a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and a quarter' reads as an overtime rate, but 'time' and 'quarter' are separate pieces and 'and a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone long in service, seasoned by many years, is old and experienced.

clue.text: Stoical, having collected a terrible bump

indicators.note: collected means gathered up together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm after taking a nasty knock on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' looks like 'suffered', but it signals a rearrangement of A TERRIBLE BUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be ruffled or upset remains calm and stoical.

clue.text: Match where, after one's tossed, team as announced comes on

indicators.note: comes on says the sounded piece follows on after the first piece

parts.note: a coin is the thing tossed at the start of a match

indicators.note: as announced means the word for team is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: At a cricket match, once the coin is tossed, the announced team takes the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like the cricket game of the surface, but it is the verb meaning to correspond. SIDE, said aloud, gives CIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that happen at the same time or agree exactly match each other.

clue.text: In confrontation with some turtles?

definitions.meaning: loggerheads are a kind of large sea turtle, so being among them is being 'at' them

explanation.definitionFit: Being in a quarrel means locked in dispute; a loggerhead is also a big-headed sea turtle, so the phrase can mean among such creatures.

clue.text: After sumo wrestling, it's the end of one timid creature

indicators.note: wrestling suggests a struggle that throws the letters of sumo about
the end of picks the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A small animal is finished off by a heavyweight wrestler.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rodent proverbially shy and fearful is a timid creature.

clue.text: Draws attention to mistakes in the score

definitions.meaning: read as points that are out: scoring that is wrong

explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to draw attention to; read whimsically, points that are wrong are mistakes in the score.

clue.text: I rose next, making strenuous efforts

indicators.note: making means forming or building something new, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone gets up next and works hard all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertions are bouts of hard physical or mental effort.

clue.text: Small boy has party piece

parts.note: Ron is a short form of a boy's name such as Ronald
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A little lad performs his party piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party piece' looks like one phrase, but 'party' is DO and 'piece' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical work with a recurring main theme is a piece of music.

clue.text: Showy marble lacking greenness

parts.note: a taw is a playing marble, especially the shooter
dry wood is seasoned, no longer green and sappy

explanation.surface: A gaudy marble lacks its green colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap and gaudy things are showy without real quality.

clue.text: Spoils the hostelry, having flies around

indicators.note: around means the word for flies is wrapped round the hostelry word

parts.note: flies, as a noun, suggests the wings of a flying insect
an inn is a hostelry, an old-fashioned pub with rooms

explanation.surface: Flies buzz round a pub and ruin its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb about the pub, but it is the noun meaning gains. 'flies' supplies WINGS, the parts a flier uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or prizes taken in a game or war count as spoils.

clue.text: Dracula, for example, I found no good at arithmetic

parts.note: Dracula is a count, a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A vampire admits he was hopeless at sums at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' and 'at' just join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning up numbers is basic arithmetic.

clue.text: "Now — Royal Marines sail!" ordered top naval sea dogs

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era, now

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commander barks an order for the marines to set sail at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the naval command of the surface, but it rearranges RM and SAIL into MIRALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior commanders of a fleet are its highest-ranking officers, old sea dogs at the top.

clue.text: Outlaw straying near edge

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A bandit wanders close to the cliff top.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor or rebel who has turned against the law or his side is an outlaw.

clue.text: He gathers force near the French riot

parts.note: G stands for the force of gravity

indicators.note: riot means wild disorder, so these letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Police force arrives near a French riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges NEAR and LE into LEANER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collects leftover grain or scraps of information gathers them up.

clue.text: A buttress it's said will hove in sight

indicators.note: it's said means the words are heard spoken aloud

parts.note: a pier is a pillar or buttress supporting a structure

explanation.surface: Engineers promise a support for the bridge will soon be visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hove in sight' is the nautical 'heave in sight', to come into view; 'will' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view, as a ship does on the horizon, is to become visible.

clue.text: Painter's cap is adjusted thus

definitions.note: Painter's reads as 'Painter is', the 's a link

indicators.note: adjusted means altered and put right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An artist tilts his beret just so.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish founder of Cubism is a famous painter.

clue.text: Said to be caricatures — goat-like characters

indicators.note: said to be means the word is judged by how it sounds spoken

parts.note: satires are works that caricature and mock their targets

explanation.surface: Cartoonists are told their caricatures make people look like goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodland gods of Greek myth, half human and half goat, are goat-like beings.

clue.text: Wrap note in one

indicators.note: in means the note word is placed inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message is wrapped up inside a single parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A linen cloth worn round the neck and shoulders by a priest is a liturgical wrap.

clue.text: Basil and rice stew can be too peppery

indicators.note: a stew mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe warns that basil and rice in a stew can taste too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peppery' looks like the taste of the stew, but it means hot-tempered; 'can be too' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A person quick to anger is hot-tempered, which is what peppery means of a person.

clue.text: Tasteless, introducing student into group

indicators.note: into means the student letter goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A new student joins a dull group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' only links; 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Food without flavour is insipid and tasteless.

clue.text: Well-known branch terminus on a railway

parts.note: a leg is a branch or section of a journey
an end is a terminus

explanation.surface: A famous branch line ends at a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch terminus' reads as one railway phrase, but it is two pieces; 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something famous enough to be the stuff of stories is well-known.

clue.text: Reportedly remained sober

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: stayed means remained

explanation.surface: Witnesses say someone stayed behind without drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serious, sedate and respectable is sober in manner.

clue.text: Angry exchanges, then second interrupts to start the duelling

indicators.note: interrupts means the letter for second breaks into the run of the other two words

parts.note: cross means angry
words are angry exchanges, as in 'having words'

explanation.surface: A heated argument turns into a sword fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry exchanges' looks like the definition, but it is two pieces; the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Duellists begin by touching blades, so the phrase means to start fighting or arguing.
